arxiv-2111-02928.title: Prediction of sunspot and plage coverage for Solar Cycle 25
arxiv-2111-02928.creator: Valentina Penza, Francesco Berrilli, Luca Bertello, Matteo Cantoresi, Serena Criscuoli
arxiv-2111-02928.description: Abstract Solar variability occurs over a broad range of spatial and temporal scales, from the Sun’s brightening over its lifetime to the fluctuations commonly associated with magnetic activity over minutes to years. The latter activity includes most prominently the 11-year sunspot solar cycle and its modulations.

arxiv-2204-04383.title: Learning-based Bounded Synthesis for Semi-MDPs with LTL Specifications
arxiv-2204-04383.creator: Ryohei Oura, Toshimitsu Ushio
arxiv-2204-04383.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ryohei Oura, Toshimitsu Ushio. This letter proposes a learning-based bounded synthesis for a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) with a linear temporal logic (LTL) specification. In the product of the SMDP and the deterministic K K -co-Büchi automaton (d K K cBA) converted from the LTL specification, we learn both the winning region of satisfying the LTL specification and the dynamics therein based on reinforcement learning and Bayesian inference. Then, we synthesize an optimal policy satisfying the following two conditions.

arxiv-2211-10447.title: Theory pipeline for PDF fitting
arxiv-2211-10447.creator: Christopher Schwan
arxiv-2211-10447.description: Abstract Fitting PDFs requires the integration of a broad range of datasets, both from data and theory side, into a unique framework. While for data the integration mainly consists in the standardization of the data format, for the theory predictions there are multiple ingredients involved.

arxiv-2403-16608.title: Vector Ising Spin Annealer for Minimizing Ising Hamiltonians
arxiv-2403-16608.creator: James S. Cummins 1 and Natalia G. Berloff
arxiv-2403-16608.description: Abstract We introduce the Vector Ising Spin Annealer (VISA), a framework in gain-based computing that harnesses light-matter interactions to solve complex optimization problems encoded in spin Hamiltonians. Traditional driven-dissipative systems often select excited states due to limitations in spin movement.

arxiv-2408-14836.title: SIMILARITY METRICS FOR LATE REVERBERATION Thanks: The work of the first author was funded by the Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering.
arxiv-2408-14836.creator: Gloria Dal Santo 1 , Karolina Prawda 1 , Sebastian J. Schlecht 2 , Vesa Välimäki 1
arxiv-2408-14836.description: Abstract Automatic tuning of reverberation algorithms relies on the optimization of a cost function. While general audio similarity metrics are useful, they are not optimized for the specific statistical properties of reverberation in rooms. This paper presents two novel metrics for assessing the similarity of late reverberation in room impulse responses.

arxiv-2504-00959.creator: Giovanni Lacopo, Claudio Gheller, Emanuele De Rubeis, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Maciej Cytowski, Luca Tornatore, Giuliano Taffoni, Ugo Varetto
arxiv-2504-00959.description: Abstract Square Kilometer Array is expected to generate hundreds of petabytes of data per year, two orders of magnitude more than current radio interferometers. arxiv-2506-10646.title: Baryon and Meson Excited States
arxiv-2506-10646.description: Abstract The masses of fifteen baryon sets and twenty-four meson sets of three or more equal-quantum excited states are fitted by a simple two-parameter logarithm function, M n = α ​ L ​ n ​ ( n ) + β M_{n}=\alpha Ln(n)+\beta , where n n is the level of radial excitation.

pmc-11359783.title: Analyzing Diabetes Detection and Classification: A Bibliometric Review (2000–2023)
pmc-11359783.creator: Jannatul Ferdaus, Esmay Azam Rochy, Uzzal Biswas, Jun Jiat Tiang, Abdullah-Al Nahid, Zeljko Zilic
pmc-11359783.description: Bibliometric analysis is a rigorous method to analyze significant quantities of bibliometric data to assess their impact on a particular field. This study used bibliometric analysis to investigate the academic research on diabetes detection and classification from 2000 to 2023. The PRISMA 2020 framework was followed to identify, filter, and select relevant papers.

pmc-11470116.title: A Multi-Decadal Hourly Coincident Wind and Solar Power Production Dataset for the Contiguous United States
pmc-11470116.creator: Allison M Campbell, Cameron Bracken, Scott Underwood, Nathalie Voisin
pmc-11470116.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As renewable energy continues its rapid expansion in the Unites States, multi-decadal hourly datasets of electricity production are needed to asses reliability and resource adequacy of power grids. Recent years have seen the release of grid-cell-level simulated meteorological variables, however these are not extended to the power domain, are not developed from a dynamically consistent numerical weather model, and only cover a historical baseline of less than a decade.

pmc-11665808.title: La contribution des militaires au paysage chirurgical canadien
pmc-11665808.creator: Chad G Ball, Edward J Harvey
pmc-11665808.description: ique mondiale grandissante, le travail des leaders de la médecine militaire est devenu extrêmement important. Ce sont eux qui prennent soin non seulement des personnes combattantes gravement blessées lors des conflits, mais aussi de la population civile se trouvant à l’intérieur ou hors des zones de guerre et qui est touchée par des traumatismes physiques et mentaux.

pmc-12655273.title: Gut Microbiotas, Plasma Metabolites, and Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis
pmc-12655273.creator: Jiayi Zhou, Zhang Fu, Yunfei Gao, Caiyan An, Zhiqiang Zhang, Xin Zhong, Liusuyan Tian, Xiuyan Yang, Junjing Zhang, Qingyuan Zhang, Dilong Wang, Ningning Li
pmc-12655273.description: Background: Previous studies have indicated that the gut microbiome and plasma metabolites play key roles in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but their causal relationships remain unclear. Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) and Mendelian randomization (MR) are powerful tools for assessing genetic causality.

pmc-13053621.title: Ameliorative Role of Silymarin in Methotrexate‐Induced Pulmonary Damage: A Multi‐Pathway Molecular Approach
pmc-13053621.creator: Aydin Genc, Emre Sahin, Eren Cankaya
pmc-13053621.description: Methotrexate (MTX) is a medication that is frequently prescribed for the treatment of both malignant disorders and inflammatory pathologies. However, its use is limited by dose‐dependent pulmonary toxicity. The present study investigated the protective effects of silymarin (SLM) against MTX‐induced lung injury by evaluating apoptosis, oxidative stress, autophagy, inflammation and histopathological changes in rats.

pmc-13159743.title: Central Canal Stenosis Severity Does Not Predict Residual Leg Pain After Percutaneous Transforaminal Endoscopic Decompression in Frail Elderly Patients: A Propensity Score-Weighted Cohort Study
pmc-13159743.creator: Miao Wang, Guang-Zhou Li, Fan-Dong Wang, Long Tang, Hao Zhang
pmc-13159743.description: PurposeSevere central canal stenosis is often considered a relative contraindication for minimally invasive decompression in frail elderly patients with lumbar spinal stenosis, yet evidence supporting this practice is limited. This study evaluated whether stenosis severity predicts persistent leg pain after percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic decompression (PTED).

pmc-13248951.title: Usability, Safety, and Diagnostic Reliability of an Automated Urinary Suction Device in Diaper-Dependent Older Adults
pmc-13248951.creator: Miho Song, Jong Hyun Yun, Hyun Young Lee, Seung Whan Doo, Ji Yeon Han, Ui Cheol Lee, Byeong Hun Jeong, Kisoo Lee, In Gab Jeong, Jae Heon Kim
pmc-13248951.description: PurposeTo evaluate the pilot clinical feasibility of an automatic urinary suction device in mobility-limited older adults, focusing on usability, functional performance, and perceived safety, and a secondary exploratory assessment of agreement between device-collected and reference urine specimens.MethodsA 2-cohort clinical evaluation was conducted.

pmc-13304404.title: Genomic and Phenotypic Characterization of Streptomyces marxii sp. nov., Producer of Kinanthraquinone B
pmc-13304404.creator: Mikhail Yu. Dobryakov, Julia A. Buyuklyan, Mikhail V. Biryukov
pmc-13304404.description: Describing novel microbial species opens access to uncharted biosynthetic gene clusters and their associated secondary metabolites, offering fresh opportunities in the search for new antibiotics urgently needed to combat multidrug resistance. In this study, we describe a new species of Streptomyces, S. marxii sp. nov. (type strain VKM Ac-3100), an actinobacterium isolated from soil in the Yaroslavl Region of Russia.

pmc-13411111.title: Perceptions of adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus about diabetes management and exercise
pmc-13411111.creator: Meera Swaminath, Stephanie A. Griggs, James Lukasik, Elias K. Spanakis, Rebecca L. Kinney, Garrett I. Ash
pmc-13411111.description: Purpose of study:The purpose of this study was to understand the experiences and challenges with diabetes management and physical activity faced by adults with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM), as well as gather feedback on proposed features for a digital health tool, to inform the development of T1DM-tailored interventions.

pmc-13556409.title: Are we missing an important point? Risk factors for intraoperative complications and additional procedures when performing post-chemotherapy RPLND for testicular tumors
pmc-13556409.creator: Mesut Altan, Hakan Keskin, Sertac Yazici
pmc-13556409.description: PurposeThis study aims to investigate the risk factors associated with additional intraoperative procedures during post-chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (PC-RPLND) in patients with advanced germ-cell tumors.Materials and MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed the data of 206 patients who underwent PC-RPLND for advanced germ-cell tumors between January 1990 and December 2022.
